title: 1891 Anglo-Manipur War and Tangkhul Pass Neutrality Pacts
title_translation: Defense of Hill Passes During the Anglo-Manipur Conflict
creator: Hunphun and Hundung Village Councils
publisher: Documented in Grimwood 1891, Hodson 1911, Manipur State Archives
notes: During the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891 following the palace uprising in Imphal, Tangkhul village councils maintained strategic defensive neutrality, safeguarding mountain passes and protecting non-combatants retreating across the eastern hills.
indigenous_tangkhul_chronicle: 1891 kum Anglo-Manipur War tharan British columns Kohima kala Tamu-wui ngathur-da Kangla chotchan.
Hunphun kala Hundung Awunga-bingna mountain passes guard sakda sovereign diplomatic neutrality maintain sakya.
Hill people-na conflict-li non-combatants-li shimlut sangda hill villages-wui destruction banish sakya.
english_translation_text: During the 1891 Anglo-Manipur War, British military columns advanced toward Kangla Palace via Kohima and Tamu through eastern hill passes.
The chiefs of Hunphun and Hundung maintained strategic diplomatic neutrality, guarding the mountain trails and securing their territories.
Tangkhul village councils granted humanitarian sanctuary to fleeing non-combatants, shielding the hill populations from military devastation.
chronicle_milestones: 1. March 1891: Palace uprising in Imphal resulting in the execution of Chief Commissioner Quinton and British officers.
2. April 1891: Three-pronged British invasion launched from Kohima, Silchar, and Tamu.
3. April 1891: Tangkhul village councils meet at Hundung pass; deliberate and enact non-belligerent defense covenants.
4. May 1891: Direct political administration established under Political Agent Major Maxwell; hill regions formally reorganized.
historical_significance: Demonstrated the strategic sovereign autonomy and diplomatic statesmanship of Tangkhul village polities during colonial conquest.

historical_terms.Khamasit-Pao: Diplomatic peace pact and non-aggression declaration
